requirements.basis: The outline plans the required changed-object distinction (weights, code, prompts/workflows versus temporary refinement), DGM and AlphaEvolve loop reconstruction, retained archive/selection, complementary Promptbreeder/SCoRe cases, baseline and task-condition matrix, transfer and negative evidence, generation/evaluation effort, and retain/revert adoption guidance. It explicitly preserves paper/code revisions and the cutoff, missing budget information, and the distinction between public implementation and replication. Requirements are otherwise mapped at an appropriate outline depth; no new experiment or extra reporting process is required. One distinct requested evaluator threat, data leakage, has no planned analysis despite a concrete DGM source passage making it consequential. I read the complete outline and original task, verified the frozen assignment and retained outline snapshot match it, and read the relevant DGM original introduction, evaluation discussion and Appendix C.3. This is requirements assessment of the outline only, not full factual validation or final-report acceptance.

findings.location: Proposed complete report item 6, with item 2 DGM reconstruction and item 5 evidence matrix
findings.basis: R_TASK expressly requires data leakage as well as adaptive overfitting. Item 6 names adaptive reuse, reference errors, reward exploitation and metric conflicts but leaves leakage unassigned. This is not merely another name for repeated selection: VSI001 original.txt, Appendix C.3 (around lines 1035-1038), says the private test patch is included in the diagnosis prompt and reports manual inspection as reassurance; its Polyglot discussion (line 111) separately discusses possible foundation-model benchmark exposure. These are relevant information-access and contamination boundaries that a transfer label alone does not settle. Add a compact planned comparison of what test/task information reaches the generator/diagnoser, what is protected, and what public evidence can establish about leakage, without demanding a new experiment or treating possible leakage as proven invalidity.
